extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), installation staff, contracting officers, staff judge advocates (SJAs), and ethics counselors involved in Army public affairs and publications
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for producing, contracting, distributing, funding, and releasing Army public affairs publications, visual information, and related media, including limits on advertising, distribution requirements, OPSEC and release authorities, and contracting/ethics rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on exclusive advertising agreements in CE contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The CE newspaper contracts will contain a provision prohibiting exclusive advertising agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No favoritism among private non-government organizations in PA products
rubrics_metrics.description: No private non-Government organization or association will be favored over another in PA products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriated funds for AF publications only when CE impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriated funds will not be used to produce AF publications unless the command has determined that a CE method is impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the CE method is impractical, publications may be procured through the installation printing facility according to AR 25–30. AF publications will not contain commercial advertisements but may contain personal classified advertising at no cost to the internal audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA office approval of news/editorial content for CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The news and editorial content of CE publications must be approved by the PA office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CE publications may contain advertising sold by the civilian printer and may include supplements or inserts. Publications and inserts become the property of the command, installation, or intended recipient upon delivery according to contract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary publications augment PA program
rubrics_metrics.description: Other AF or CE publications augment the PA program, e.g., base and installation guides (with or without telephone directories) and maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a record copy of each publication issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PA office and post library will maintain a record copy (AR 25–400–2) of each issue of every publication produced under this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify editorials vs. commentaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications will distinguish between editorials (command position) and commentaries (personal opinion) by clearly identifying them as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult legal/provost marshal on legal notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Local SJA and the installation provost marshal should be consulted for current guidance on placing legal notices required by Federal and state laws in Army PA publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory distribution and mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All Army PA publications are mailed in envelopes only. First-Class mail is used for required mailing. The PAOs of CE publications should have the printer make the mandatory distribution. Required numbers of copies of each issue must be mailed to specified addresses (HQDA, AFIS, DINFOS, State Historical Society of Wisconsin, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders will mail copies as required by their ACOM. Official mail may be used for ARNG and USAR newspapers at the cheapest rate possible to home addresses; attempt to have CE contractor distribute as many as possible. Follow distribution guidance from FORSCOM, TRADOC, NGB as applicable. Publications may also be distributed through official channels and placed in racks/stands in high-traffic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on types of publications printed under this regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsletters, information bulletins, training publications, and similar publications are defined by AR 25–30 and will not be printed under the provisions of this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE publications are sole PA publications allowed regular paid advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CE publications authorized by this regulation are the only Army PA publications allowed to contain paid advertisements on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The morale, welfare, and recreation (MWR) may sell advertising under some circumstances outlined in DODI 1015.10, enclosure 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation to conserve resources
rubrics_metrics.description: To conserve resources, installations will consolidate safety, personnel, and other widely distributed bulletins into the post newspaper, as feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-purpose publications policy and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Special-purpose publications (exercises, contingency operations, special missions, overseas deployments, summer camps) will be incorporated into exercise/training planning; normally only one publication under one name will be published during each event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commander directing publication will notify ASCC/ACOM/DRU PAO with date, name, frequency, printed circulation, page count, and purpose. One copy of each issue must be sent to unit’s ASCC/ACOM/DRU PAO, hosting command PAO, and OCPA. Exercise/training PA evaluator or publication program manager will evaluate special-purpose publications at least once during publication period and include copies in the after action report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of original visual information materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All original visual information materials or requirements for visual information products, services, and capabilities meeting criteria for record documentation will be processed according to AR 25–1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders or PAOs wishing to produce or revise visual information products must submit requests to the local service provider or multimedia/visual information manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of commercially leased/purchased visual information
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual information products that are commercially leased, rented, or purchased are controlled by the DOIM at the installation level and the Deputy Chief of Staff for Information Management and/or ACOM visual information manager at ASCC/ACOM/DRU level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution rules for non-DOD commercial publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will afford reputable distributors of other publications the opportunity to sell or give away publications at the activities they command but requests from civilian publishers to distribute materials not produced under Government regulations will be considered solicitations and referred to the staff agency implementing AR 210–7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such publications will not be distributed through official channels and will be placed only in stands or racks provided by the publisher in general use areas. The publisher must properly maintain the stand/rack. Care must be taken to protect exclusive distribution rights of authorized CE publications. Paid subscriptions may be hand delivered door-to-door according to AR 210–7 and local policies. Commanders may prohibit distribution of non-DOD publications detrimental to morale, illegal, or violating this regulation. Installations are usually nonpublic forums; first amendment rights do not guarantee distribution access—commanders must stipulate controlled distribution by location and quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA funding authority and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: DFAS 37–100 provides fiscal authority on funding of PA activities. Personnel should consult the command or activity resource management office for clarification and guidance on funding issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of PA funds
rubrics_metrics.description: PA funds may be used to defray costs of PA activities that are part of the command’s approved PA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding requirements may include civilian pay, travel, printing, contracts, supplies, speaking engagements, support for civic ceremonies, public announcements of Army support to community events, and web publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to PA funds use
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions: use of Army resources to support public events will be at no additional cost to the Government; costs for Army participation in public events will be paid by event sponsors; costs the Army would have incurred notwithstanding support are not reimbursable (e.g., local travel, local telephone calls, aviation fuel when provided as part of ongoing training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs eligible for unprogrammed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army will pay all unprogrammed costs of supporting PA programs specifically authorized by public law, executive order, Secretary of Defense, or SECARMY; and certain programs when in DA's primary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: official Federal Government functions, Army or civic-sponsored observances of national holidays (AFD/AFW), official civil ceremonies/functions, official speaking engagements, events in national/professional/scientific/technical interest when approved by OCPA, and direct support of recruiting when charged to recruiting funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events qualifying for PA funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that may be funded if participation is in the best interest of the Army and funds available: official Federal Government functions; public observances of national holidays; national conventions of veterans associations; official civil ceremonies; speaking engagements; activities supporting recruiting including ROTC; appearances/demonstrations by special units; other events in national interest approved by SecDef or unified combatant commander; local events within PA area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor payment required for events outside funding criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Army organizations may participate in events that do not meet funding criteria if event sponsors pay associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional costs normally include travel/transportation of personnel/equipment; meals/lodging/per diem; transportation/handling/aviation fuel; exhibit space/rental/utilities/custodial services; public liability and property damage insurance; other services per agreement. Using routine training transport may be considered Army share. PA funds will not be expended for hosting/representational purposes (luncheons, dinners, theater tickets, gifts); official hosting expenses may only be charged to SECARMY’s contingency fund per AR 37–47. OMA funds may pay incidental costs when sponsor agrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance guidelines for PA funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds programmed and expended for PA activities are part of each component’s OMA account; funding will be kept to the minimum necessary to accomplish Army objectives and beyond OMA funds PA activities will be at no additional cost to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA funds may be used to purchase/distribute promotional items within DOD 5500.7–R limits; promotional items must clearly support the mission/PA objectives. Financing done according to DA PPBE (see AR 1–1). Reimbursement procedures in DFAS–IN 37–1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising costs for environmental hearing notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Events and activities required by environmental laws such as environmental hearings will be paid with funds from the environmental program budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to contract for PA services and products
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs may contract with commercial firms for services and products; contracts will be let according to applicable laws, regulations, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting requirements for CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are authorized to contract in writing for CE publications; oral contracts are not acceptable. The command will guarantee first publication and distribution of locally produced editorial content; publication should become the property of the command/installation/upon delivery per contract terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines in DODI 5120.4. CE newspaper contracting not subject to FAR because appropriated funds are not used, though commanders may use FAR procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting gratuities from CE contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Army military and civilian personnel are prohibited from soliciting or accepting any gratuity from a current or prospective CE contractor. Family members may also be prohibited. Consult servicing SJA for guidance (see 5 CFR 2635.202(a) and DOD 5500.7–R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment and conflict-of-interest rules for CE contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid appearance of conflict, Army personnel whose duties involve selection/approval of a CE contractor or production/distribution may not accept off-duty employment with any prospective bidder or CE printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel required by law to disqualify themselves from participating in official matters that might affect a CE contractor with whom a family member or business partner has a relationship. Those who cannot discharge responsibilities may face reassignment unless relationship is terminated. Commanders and PAOs should consult ethics counselors when potential conflicts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost rules for CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The command will pay travel costs incurred by Government personnel to create or review material for use in the CE publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government personnel will not accept reimbursement for transportation, accommodations, meals, gratuities, or other incidentals from the CE contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with contracting officer on CE contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel must coordinate with the command’s contracting officer for contract requirements and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting for Army-funded publications: editorial control and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: AF publications normally printed by civilian printer under contract or in Government printing facilities. The editorial content and distribution are accomplished by contracting command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseas AF newspapers authorized under contract with Stars and Stripes; other printing methods evaluated case-by-case. Using four-color process is authorized if commander and PAO determine it enhances communication. AF publications will not carry commercial advertising but may include nonpaid personal listings and noncommercial news/announcements regarding MWR/commissaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PAD for Army-funded video/TV production contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will use the Production Acquisition Division (PAD), Army Multimedia and Visual Information Directorate, as the primary source for establishing multimedia and television production contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAD will ensure FAR-required rights and data clauses are included so the Army owns all rights and master materials. The Army will not pay royalties, recurring license or run-time fees, use tax, or similar additional payments. Organizations will use PAD contracts regardless of dollar value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and mailing rules for Army-funded publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail and distribution costs must be kept to a minimum consistent with timeliness and postal regulations. Army newspapers may be distributed through official channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD Postage and Fees Paid indicia may be used for mandatory distribution, PA office/admin purposes, chain-of-command mailings, bulk mailing to subordinate units, complimentary copies, and one unsolicited request response if in best interest. PAOs may use appropriated funds to mail copies when mailed for official reasons as determined by commander. CE contractors will not use official postage. Army newspapers mailed as controlled circulation Third/Fourth Class or Third Class bulk. Mailing by CE contractors should be included in CE contract; printers may charge reasonable postage/handling fee for approved requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for security review prior to public release
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD policy requires any official information intended for public release that pertains to military matters, national security issues, or subjects of significant concern to the DOD be cleared by appropriate security review and PA offices prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes materials placed on the Internet or released via similar electronic media. Prior unofficial publication does not constitute authority for official release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial and objective dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about policies of the United States and its allies will be disseminated impartially and objectively, according to local command guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information requiring OSD/OCPA clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that meets specified criteria (e.g., originates at Seat of Government; potential national/international interest; foreign policy implications; high-level DOD policy; subjects of controversy among Services or with Federal agencies; initial info on new weapons or significant military operations; communications security; lists of names of sensitive/unit personnel; casualty info on key personnel; activation/inactivation of brigade+ units; DOD counterterrorist activities; etc.) must be submitted to OCPA for OSD clearance prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doubtful cases also submitted. See full list in regulation (items 1–20+) for specific categories that require clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQDA OCPA authority and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The OCPA has authority to release information about the Army as a whole and will coordinate with OCLL and other DA staff agencies as appropriate on replies to congressional inquiries and other transmittals with significant PA implications. Interviews and press conferences at the Pentagon are arranged by OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authority for commanders below HQDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders below HQDA level are authorized to release information wholly within their mission/scope and not restricted by higher-level provisions, normally via the PAO who prepares material and ensures security review. PAO will grant clearance or forward to appropriate headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must inform OCPA through command channels when national media requests or situations with potential national exposure occur. Local commanders have flexibility but should alert OCPA when national media interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid release coordination during crisis/emerging events
rubrics_metrics.description: If a crisis or emerging event occurs in an area of PA responsibility, the first PAO contacted or on the scene will ensure appropriate information is released as quickly as possible to pertinent audiences and coordinate with the next higher headquarters to define PA responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on releasing intelligence/security/ARSOF operational information
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing military intelligence and security related information, photographs, and video/audiotapes must be authorized by INSCOM; releasing operational information on all ARSOFs will be coordinated with USASOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding information and OPSEC review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguarded information will not be discussed, shown, or made available to unauthorized individuals. All Army personnel must be aware of and support the Army’s OPSEC program. Information, materials, or records must be reviewed for OPSEC considerations in accordance with AR 530–1 prior to public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff office or agency providing information to the PA office should accomplish OPSEC reviews. Additionally, releasable information must be accurate and adhere to published DOD and Army policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of Army records and FOIA-related guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Army records will only be released when approved by the appropriate authority in accordance with AR 25–55 and AR 340–21. Officials releasing records will inform PAOs if records contain controversial information; PAOs will notify commanders and contact OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records releasable under FOIA should be released to media representatives when requested through PA channels to provide timely information and avoid invoking FOIA formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate to all audiences and tailored outreach methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are responsible for providing information within their units; PA personnel assist, advise, plan, train, and conduct PA operations. Commanders should consider methods such as quarterly commander calls, open houses, sensing sessions, Family support group meetings, formal/informal discussions with civilian professional groups, writing articles, public speaking, and participating in local community affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs will assess/evaluate audiences via sensing sessions, focus groups, surveys, or interviews. Creators/designers of Internet/Intranet material must ensure OPSEC requirements are met. Commanders must be aware of subgroups (first-term Soldiers, NCOs, officers, spouses, children, civilians, ROTC, retirees, local nationals) and their unique information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with state and local officials for major proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Within national security and congressional constraints, state and local officials must be consulted at the earliest stages of planning/developing major policy, budget, or reorganization proposals that have significant state/local impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCPA will provide consultation guidance to ASCC/ACOM/DRU and activities; no early consultation will take place without HQDA guidance. Commands should advise HQDA OCPA and OCLL of local or congressional issues via local PAO and congressional affairs contact officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual information support and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Official photography, television, audio, and graphic art support to public information programs is authorized, but recording/reproducing is kept to the minimum required to satisfy official needs and photographic/video coverage of VIP visits is restricted to minimum essential requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using PA resources to produce documentation or visual/written records for Soldier’s use is authorized in a limited capacity when not interfering with PA's primary mission (examples: farewell books, slideshows, videos). The PA is authorized to take news-related photographs only; using PA resources for non-newsworthy promotion boards, ceremonies, or social events is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating media visits and ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: News media representatives may visit installation areas normally open to the public when subject matter is of local interest or deals with spontaneous news events and the information is releasable. Media restricted from areas requiring control for criminal justice purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media coverage of controversial or national-interest subjects will be coordinated through channels to OCPA. Installations must develop local procedures for handling media during disaster/civil disturbance. Commanders and media will establish ground rules to ensure free flow of information while safeguarding classified/sensitive information. PA personnel will not use physical force or confiscate media equipment; violations reported to appropriate authorities immediately.
